What AIQ means for Indian retailers



“The retailer who knows their customer best will win. AI is, for the first time in history, making it possible for every retailer to know every customer best.”

India’s retail market, the world's fifth-largest and growing at over 10 per cent annually, is being reshaped by AI at a pace outpacing most organisations’ ability to respond. From hyper-personalised product recommendations to AI-driven supply chains and dynamic pricing, the retailers building the highest AI quotient are redefining the consumer relationship.Consider what a customer interaction looks like for a high-AIQ Indian retailer today. A consumer opens an app and is presented with a homepage configured in real time based on their purchase history, browsing behaviour, time of day, location, and current inventory availability.The product they are most likely to buy surfaces first. The price they are offered reflects their price sensitivity, their loyalty profile, and competitive pricing intelligence. The delivery promise they receive is generated by an AI system that has assessed current logistics capacity, their location, and historical delivery performance in their pin code.It is the operational reality for India’s most advanced retail organisations. And for those who have not built this capability, the gap is widening every quarter.The evidence of AI’s impact on retail business performance is compelling and consistent across geographies.Sales professionals using AI are 47 per cent more productive, saving an average of 12 hours a week. In 2024, 83% of sales teams that used AI reported revenue growth, compared with 66% of those that did not. Sales professionals who use AI weekly have 78 per cent shorter deal cycles.The gains in customer experience are equally well documented. A Salesforce survey found that 63% of service professionals feel that generative AI helps them get work done faster. McKinsey data indicates that customer operations is one of the four most valuable areas for AI applications, with AI-enabled customer operations achieving 82 per cent faster response times. This is a structural competitive advantage for early movers in India’s retail space, where customer service quality has traditionally been a differentiator.Overstocking and understocking are the twin pathologies of retail inventory management. The cost of carrying excess inventory in Indian retail is substantial, while the cost of a stockout, which includes lost sales, customer disappointment, and potential permanent churn, is even higher.AI-driven demand forecasting systems trained on historical sales data, real-time market signals, seasonal patterns, promotional calendars, and macroeconomic indicators are contributing to improvements in forecast accuracy that can directly translate into margin.The Indian AI market in the supply chain, which includes retail logistics and inventory management,, is projected to grow at a CAGR of 37.8 per cent through 2032. The e-commerce sector is a primary driver, with companies leveraging AI to manage high order volumes, optimise last-mile delivery, and improve customer satisfaction.The traditional retail marketing model, which includes mass communication, broad targeting, and standard promotions, is being replaced by AI-powered personalisation that treats every customer as a segment of one. McKinsey’s analysis of AI’s impact on marketing found that AI-powered personalised messaging and pipeline management are among the highest-return AI applications in the marketing function.For Indian retailers operating in a market of 1.4 billion people with extraordinary demographic, linguistic, and cultural diversity, personalisation at scale represents both the greatest challenge and the greatest opportunity. A high-AIQ retailer does not communicate with its customers in Hindi, English or Tamil. It communicates with each customer in the language of their individual preferences, purchase history, and life context.India’s retail landscape is uniquely complex: a massive and growing e-commerce sector co-exists with 12 million traditional kirana stores, modern trade formats, and a rapidly expanding quick-commerce segment. The consumer moves fluidly between these channels, expecting a seamless experience in each. AI is the only technology capable of creating and managing this seamlessness at scale by unifying the data from every customer touchpoint into a single intelligence layer that informs every subsequent interaction.Fifty-three per cent of small business owners across sectors report noticeable improvements in customer experience after implementing AI solutions. For India’s large retail organisations, which can deploy more sophisticated AI systems and generate more data to train them, the potential impact is correspondingly greater.A high-AIQ retail organisation has moved beyond using AI as a tool for operational efficiency and built it as the foundation of its customer relationship. It knows its customers better than any competitor. It serves them faster and more relevantly. It manages its inventory and supply chain with a level of precision that manual processes cannot match. And it does all of this at a scale and cost that creates a structural advantage.The TOI AI Quotient Awards invite India’s retail leaders from the country’s largest e-commerce platforms to the most innovative traditional retailers and D2C brands to demonstrate the AI Quotient they have built. The award is for organisations that have made the customer relationship genuinely smarter through AI.
Article Summary: India’s retail market, the world's fifth-largest and growing at over 10 per cent annually, is being reshaped by AI. Sales professionals using AI are 47 per cent more productive, saving an average of 12 hours a week. McKinsey data indicates that customer operations is one of the four most valuable areas for AI applications.

Article Title: One of China's biggest ecommerce company to employees: Starting July 10, you cannot use America's ...
Article Text:
Accusations of backdoor Access

Reddit post claims spyware concerns

Dispute over data scraping

One of China’s largest ecommerce companies, Alibaba has announced that starting July 10, 2026, employees will be prohibited from using Anthropic’s Claude Code in office environment. According to a report by Chinese publication Yicai, this decision made by Alibaba follows internal assessments which flagged that the tool has ‘high-risk software’ after reports suggested it contained potential backdoors. The report also suggests that Alibaba has added Claude Code to its restricted software list and is also recommending employees to use Qoder as an alternative.According to another report by a Dutch publication, Techzine, Alibaba has accused Anthropic of embedding a backdoor into Claude Code, raising alarms about potential unauthorised access to sensitive corporate data. The report also noted that the alleged mechanism was first flagged by a Reddit user who claimed to have reverse-engineered Claude Code. Starting with version 2.1.91, the tool allegedly checked proxy configurations and time zones against hidden lists of Chinese corporate networks and AI labs, including Alibaba, Baidu, ByteDance, and Moonshot AI.Anthropic has not issued a formal statement, though a Claude Code team member said the mechanism was intended to combat account sales and model distillation, and promised it would be removed in the next release.A widely circulated Reddit post alleged that Claude Code contained embedded spyware, sparking fears about surveillance and data security. While unverified, the claims added fuel to growing skepticism across Asia’s tech sector and contributed to Alibaba’s decision to blacklist the tool.“Since version 2.1.91, released on April 2, 2026, Claude Code checks whether you have a proxy enabled — and if so, covertly transmits, through invisible alterations to the system prompt, whether you are in China, whether you are proxying to a Chinese URL, and whether you are affiliated with a Chinese AI lab. Anthropic further attempted to obfuscate this code within the Claude Code binary,” reads the Reddit post.“Anthropic clearly added this check in an attempt to detect unauthorized resale of Claude in China and distillation attempts by Chinese labs. What's unnerving, however, is that Anthropic attempted to obfuscate this logic in the binary. Much of it is XOR-obfuscated with the key 91, likely to prevent it from showing up in a plain strings dump. Furthermore, the release notes for version 2.1.91 make absolutely no mention of this check. Their intent is also clear in how they hide this with steganography in the system prompt, making small variations that are imperceptible to any user — and perhaps even to the model — but are easily detectable by Anthropic,” added the Reddit post.The controversy comes amid a broader conflict between the two companies. In June, Anthropic accused Alibaba’s Qwen lab of running nearly 25,000 fraudulent accounts to scrape Claude outputs, amounting to 28.8 million interactions. Alibaba’s latest move to block Claude Code internally is seen as a counter-accusation, intensifying tensions between US and Chinese AI firms.
Article Summary: Alibaba has banned employees from using Anthropic's Claude Code in office environment. The move follows reports that the tool has 'high-risk software' and could contain spyware. Anthropic has not issued a formal statement, though a Claude Code team member said the mechanism was intended to combat account sales and model distillation.

Article Title: Protecting the kids: Majority of Americans support banning social media for children under 16, says report
Article Text:
Support spans across the country



Nearly 60% of American adults support a total ban on social media use for children under the age of 16, according to a major new study released by the Pew Research Center. The survey was conducted from May 26 to June 1, and it highlights growing public anger over how digital platforms impact the mental health and well-being of young people. At a time when tech companies face scrutiny over youth safety features, the data by the study reveals that approximately one-in-five adults oppose a ban, while a quarter remain undecided. According to the current standard across most tech platforms, users need to be at least 13 years old to open an account.The support varies across demographics. Adults with children under the age of 18 are significantly more likely to favour a ban than those without minor children. While roughly half or more of every single age demographic supports the restriction, Americans aged 30 to 49 are the most eager to see the under-16 ban put into law.The perspective comes as governments around the world are drafting laws to enforce strict digital boundaries for teenagers. Australia, Canada and the UK have already established or are actively deliberating a statutory minimum age of 16 for all social media access.Inside the US, state lawmakers in California are moving forward with similar statewide legislation.While a total ban under 16 commands a clear majority, even larger numbers of Americans are demanding immediate, everyday guardrails for minors who are legally allowed online.According to Pew’s tracking data, public support for platform regulations has surged over the past three years. About 85% of adults believe social media companies must mandate parental consent before a minor can create an account, up from 81% in 2023.Additionally, 78% of respondents want platforms to enforce strict daily time limits for minors and require users to legally verify their age before logging in. Across all three tracking categories, about 10% of Americans expressed any opposition to the regulations.
Article Summary: Nearly 60% of American adults support a total ban on social media use for children under the age of 16, according to a major new study released by the Pew Research Center. Approximately one-in-five adults oppose a ban, while a quarter remain undecided. According to the current standard across most tech platforms, users need to be at least 13 years old to open an account.

Article Title: Amazon confirms custom AI chips for its devices, devices head Panos Panay says ‘wait’ for what comes next
Article Text:
Amazon is making its own chips



Alexa+ and the push to tie it all together



‘A lab full of AI devices'



Amazon is building its own artificial intelligence (AI) chips for the devices it ships into millions of homes, and the company’s top hardware executive says that is the beginning of a much bigger vision for what AI-powered gadgets may look like. Panos Panay, Amazon's head of devices and services, has talked about e-commerce giant’s semiconductor strategy in an interview with CNBC, revealing details about custom chip efforts and future AI devices.Amazon’s custom silicon is already inside some of its most popular products, including the Echo Show 8, Echo Show 11, and Fire TV devices. In October, the company unveiled the AZ3 and AZ3 Pro chips, designed specifically to run AI models directly on the device.“We do make our own end-to-end silicon for the devices that we ship,” Panay said, clarifying why owning the chip design matters so much for Amazon's ambitions.“If we're going to go deliver this ambient experience in the home for people in the most secure way, we definitely need to think about how that end-to-end delivery of hardware comes together. If you really want that hardware and software connection — on some of the more critical devices right now, our focus is end-to-end silicon,” he saidNotably, Panay noted that Amazon continues to use chips from third-party suppliers like Qualcomm for some devices.The chip strategy is closely tied to Amazon's broader AI ambitions, centred on Alexa+, the upgraded version of its digital assistant that became generally available in the US this year. Alexa+ is designed to handle complex, multi-step queries, learn from context, and understand user patterns over time. Amazon aims to connect its entire ecosystem into one intelligent experience that gets smarter the more you use it.Panay also gave a sneak peek into what’s Amazon is building.“I think we might be moving away from a world of apps and screens,” Panay said, suggesting that conversation and context will become the primary way people interact with AI assistants.“When you think about the future of AI devices, you've got to be super sceptical right now for anyone who tells you they know what they are. I have a lab full of devices," he said, essentially confirming “a whole roadmap of on-the-go devices” that people carry with them, that collect data passively and that people talk to naturally throughout the day.“So when you are back in the home or when you are at work, that connection stays consistent and contextual,” Panay said.
Article Summary: Amazon is building its own artificial intelligence (AI) chips for the devices it ships into millions of homes. The company’s top hardware executive says that is the beginning of a much bigger vision for what AI-powered gadgets may look like. The chip strategy is closely tied to Amazon's broader AI ambitions, centred on Alexa+.

Anthropic is reportedly renegotiating the pricing terms of its artificial intelligence (AI) models with one of its earliest investors, Amazon . A report claims that Amazon may have to pay more to use Anthropic's AI models after the AI startup revised part of its commercial agreement with the tech giant. Anthropic may have shifted Amazon's pricing structure from computing hours to AI tokens, a change expected to take effect next year, the report notes.According to a report by The Information, the new arrangement could increase Amazon's costs for using Anthropic's AI models across products, including Alexa for Shopping, Kiro and Quick. The report added that Amazon is even evaluating alternative AI models, including OpenAI 's models and its in-house Nova models, to help manage potential cost increases.The report even highlighted that Amazon has been working to reduce its dependence on Anthropic's models. AWS executives have reportedly expressed concerns that several Amazon products rely on Anthropic's technology instead of the company's own Nova models. Amazon has also introduced options that let customers choose among multiple AI models available through Amazon Bedrock. Depending on the task, the platform can select an appropriate model based on factors including cost and speed.Jiggar Thakkar, vice president of agentic AI for business at AWS, reportedly said in an interview. As per the report, Anthropic and Amazon have also collaborated on technical development, including software contributions that helped improve the usability of Amazon's Trainium AI chips.Responding to the report, Amazon denied that the revised agreement would increase its expenses. An Amazon spokesperson said,Meanwhile, Anthropic said that while billing models have changed for some customers, the overall cost of using its AI models has continued to decline.an Anthropic spokesperson said.According to the report, Amazon previously paid Anthropic based on the number of computing hours consumed by its AI models. Under the revised agreement, charges will instead be based on the number of tokens processed, the standard unit for measuring AI model usage. The report noted that Anthropic has also moved other customers from seat-based pricing to usage-based pricing this year, resulting in higher costs for some users.Amazon and Anthropic have maintained a strategic partnership since 2023, when Amazon invested $4 billion in the AI company. As part of the agreement, Anthropic selected Amazon Web Services (AWS) as its primary cloud provider and began using Amazon's Trainium and Inferentia AI chips.Earlier this year, Amazon also agreed to invest up to an additional $25 billion in Anthropic. Anthropic may have shifted Amazon's pricing structure from computing hours to AI tokens.

Article Title: Zurich has become a secret AI powerhouse, with Google, Apple, and OpenAI in a city of just 400,000, and the reason is a rare mix of talent, stability, and speed
Article Text:
Zurich skyline during blue hour | Wikimedia Commons

Zurich skyline during blue hour | Wikimedia Commons

Why global tech giants keep choosing Zurich

A deep-tech economy built for artificial intelligence

ETH Zurich | Wikimedia Commons

Universities are fueling the AI talent pipeline

A collaborative ecosystem that’s difficult to replicate

Not replacing Silicon Valley, but complementing it

Silicon Valley may still dominate headlines, but another city is quietly becoming one of the world’s most influential artificial intelligence hubs. With a population of just over 400,000, Zurich has attracted research and development centers from some of the biggest names in technology, including Apple, Google, Meta, Microsoft, NVIDIA, OpenAI, Anthropic and Disney Research. What started as Google’s decision to establish its largest engineering hub outside the United States has evolved into one of the world’s densest ecosystems for AI research, talent and commercialization. Instead of competing directly with Silicon Valley, Zurich has carved out a distinct role by combining world-class research, political stability, and an innovation-first economy that continues to draw global technology companies.One of Zurich’s biggest advantages is its location. Situated in the heart of Europe, the Greater Zurich Area provides companies with easy access to major European markets while offering the political stability and regulatory certainty that many businesses value when investing in long-term research, according to the Greater Zurich Area Official Website . Switzerland is also known for its strong intellectual property protections, making it an attractive destination for companies developing advanced AI technologies.Zurich Airport further strengthens the region’s appeal by connecting businesses directly with major cities across Europe, North America and Asia.The country’s broader innovation credentials reinforce that reputation. According to WIPO , Switzerland has ranked first in the Global Innovation Index for more than a decade, reflecting its consistent investment in research, education, and technological development. The country spends more than 3% of its GDP on research and development, while Google recently committed $1 million to support the Swiss National AI Institute, highlighting growing confidence in Switzerland’s AI ecosystem.Unlike many technology hubs that prioritize rapid scaling, Switzerland has built its economy around specialized, knowledge-intensive industries. Although salaries and operating costs are relatively high by European standards, they remain significantly lower than comparable roles in Silicon Valley. More importantly, companies operating in Zurich are often less concerned with assembling the largest workforce and more focused on recruiting highly specialized engineers and researchers capable of developing frontier technologies.This emphasis is reflected in Switzerland’s investment landscape. More than 60% of Swiss venture capital flows into deep-tech startups, the highest proportion of any major economy. According to the Swiss Deep Tech Report 2026, Switzerland also leads Europe in deep-tech investment per capita, underscoring the country’s long-term commitment to science-driven innovation. Instead of chasing short-term growth, investors have increasingly backed companies working in robotics, artificial intelligence, biotechnology and advanced computing, creating an ecosystem designed for breakthrough research rather than rapid expansion.At the center of Zurich’s success is an unusually close relationship between academia and industry. Institutions such as ETH Zurich, the University of Zurich, EPFL, SUPSI, and ZHAW consistently produce graduates who move seamlessly between universities, startups, and global technology companies. Engineers working at Google frequently collaborate with ETH Zurich, while graduates regularly join firms such as Anthropic, Microsoft and OpenAI before launching startups of their own.The numbers reflect this concentration of expertise. According to the Stanford AI Index 2026 , Switzerland ranks first globally for AI researchers and inventors per capita, outperforming countries including Singapore, Sweden and the United States. ETH Zurich alone generated more than 40 spin-offs and startups in 2025, reinforcing its reputation as one of Europe’s leading engines for deep-tech entrepreneurship. Meanwhile, former Google Switzerland employees have gone on to establish roughly 210 companies and create around 2,600 jobs over the past two decades, illustrating how knowledge continues circulating throughout the local ecosystem rather than leaving it.What truly distinguishes Zurich is not simply the presence of major technology companies, but the density of connections between them. Researchers, investors, founders, and corporate leaders frequently collaborate through professional networks, university partnerships, and industry events, allowing ideas to move quickly from laboratories to commercial applications.That collaboration is increasingly visible through initiatives such as the Zurich AI Festival, which brings together thousands of researchers, entrepreneurs, policymakers and investors to discuss everything from AI governance and healthcare to creativity and environmental sustainability. The festival reflects Zurich’s growing ambition to become not only a center for AI development, but also a global venue for shaping conversations around responsible artificial intelligence.Despite its growing influence, Zurich is not trying to replace Silicon Valley. Instead, many companies view the two ecosystems as complementary. Silicon Valley remains the global leader in venture capital, startup financing and frontier AI model development, while Zurich offers something equally valuable: immediate access to elite researchers, leading universities, industrial partners and sectors where precision, regulation and reliability are essential.For companies building the next generation of AI products, geography has become a strategic advantage. In Zurich, the distance between groundbreaking academic research, specialized talent, venture capital, and real-world deployment is often measured in minutes rather than hours. That rare combination has transformed a relatively small Swiss city into one of the world’s most influential AI powerhouses, proving that scale alone is no longer the defining factor in global technological leadership.
Article Summary: Zurich has attracted research and development centers from some of the biggest names in technology, including Apple, Google, Meta, Microsoft, NVIDIA, OpenAI, Anthropic and Disney Research. Instead of competing directly with Silicon Valley, Zurich has carved out a distinct role by combining world-class research and political stability.

Article Title: Animated stamps from USC celebrate 14 builders of the modern internet, from DNS and video calls to JPEG, encryption, and the algorithms inside phones
Article Text:
A promotional banner titled "AMERICA 250. CELEBRATING TROJAN COMPUTING BUILDERS." It features a grid of 14 mock commemorative U.S. postage stamps, each honoring a legendary USC computer scientist, engineer, or innovator. Image Credit: USC Information Sciences Institute

Another way to mark the United States’ 250th anniversary is through USC's animated stamp series

The inventions that make everyday internet possible

Technological innovations extending further than the computers

A promotional banner titled "AMERICA 250. CELEBRATING TROJAN COMPUTING BUILDERS." It features a grid of 14 mock commemorative U.S. postage stamps, each honoring a legendary USC computer scientist, engineer, or innovator. Image Credit: USC Information Sciences Institute

Algorithms behind modern-day artificial intelligence

Unrecognised pioneers of commonly used technology

Whether you type a website address, video-call a distant friend, or unlock a phone with your face or fingerprint, many everyday digital tools trace back to discoveries made decades ago. However, a newly released animated stamp series aims to pay homage to the engineers and computer scientists behind some of these inventions.In light of the 250 years since America's formation, the University of Southern California (USC) is releasing a series of 14 animated digital stamps to commemorate the researchers, alumni, and professors whose inventions played a crucial role in shaping the contemporary computing environment. These stamps will not be official US Postal Service stamps.In this time of the US Postal Service celebrating the nation’s semiquincentennial through their own official stamps that have been recently released as the American Icons series curated by fashion designer Ralph Lauren.USC's version takes a different approach. The stamps honor scientists whose innovations became embedded in modern technology, often without users realizing it.Among the best-known names mentioned is Jon Postel, described as an architect of the early Internet.At USC's Information Sciences Institute, Postel managed internet address assignment and edited the Request for Comments (RFC), which still defines internet protocols today.Another honoree is Paul Mockapetris, who created the Domain Name System (DNS), introduced in 1983 at USC's Information Sciences Institute. The technology lets users reach websites by typing easy-to-remember names instead of long numerical IP addresses. The Internet Society describes DNS as one of the basic building blocks of the Internet.Eve Schooler, the inventor of the Session Initiation Protocol (SIP), also known as the 'voice of the internet,' is included in the series. The protocol is extensively used in setting up and controlling internet voice and video calls.The series also highlights technological innovations that go well beyond the internet.William Pratt is credited with inventing transform coding, which became a basis for JPEG image compression and MPEG video compression. Both greatly reduced file sizes while preserving quality, helping make digital photography and video practical on the internet. Another invention highlighted is Andrew Viterbi's Viterbi algorithm, which plays an important role in decoding digital signals used in wireless communications.Cybersecurity is also represented by Leonard Adleman, who co-invented RSA, one of the most widely used public-key cryptography systems. The invention is behind today's secure internet banking, communications, and many other internet security systems. Adleman won the 2002 ACM A.M. Turing Award for these achievements.Also honored is Richard Bellman, whose work on dynamic programming remains important in optimization and reinforcement learning. Bellman's dynamic programming methods continue to be widely used in artificial intelligence, robotics, and economics for decision-making problems. Reportedly, dynamic programming is one of the most important optimization methods in computer science.Other honorees include robotics researcher Maja Matarić, who developed socially assistive robots for healthcare, and George Bekey, who helped establish robotics as a major field of study.Although well-known figures such as Apple co-founder Mike Markkula are included, most of the recognition goes to scientists whose achievements happened behind the scenes.From DNS managing the internet traffic, RSA securing monetary transactions, JPEG reducing photos, to algorithms used in phones for the processing of wireless signals - all of these inventions are so ingrained in the modern reality that people do not usually give any thought about the creators of such technologies.USC's animated stamps show how decades of work by engineers and computer scientists produced technologies that are now widely used, even if the scientists themselves remain little known.
Article Summary: USC has released a series of 14 animated digital stamps to commemorate the researchers, alumni, and professors whose inventions played a crucial role in shaping the contemporary computing environment. Among the best-known names mentioned is Jon Postel, described as an architect of the early Internet. The series also highlights technological innovations that go well beyond the internet.

Article Title: Elon Musk’s two-word strong clarification on reports that SpaceX showcased AI device to investors
Article Text:
What the report claimed



Elon Musk has responded to a media reports which claimed that SpaceX is secretly developing a physical artificial intelligence (AI) device, and that his aerospace company recently demonstrated an early prototype of this handheld AI device to a select group of high-profile investors ahead of a massive initial public offering (IPO). A report published by The Wall Street Journal also claimed that the device would run on a custom, proprietary operating system and rely on advanced AI from Musk’s AI startup, xAI.Musk, however, wasted no time in ‘killing’ the rumor mill, issuing a blunt, two-word clarification on X (formerly Twitter) to dismiss the allegations: “Utterly False”.According to the report, the alleged concept device was described as an incredibly thin handset – even slimmer than Apple’s current iPhone. The report further said that the hardware is powered by a Qualcomm Snapdragon processor and has been designed to reshape how humans interact with AI, serving as a physical gateway for Musk's xAI chatbot.Citing sources, the report noted that SpaceX pitched the project to investors as an early-stage concept that would help Musk bypass the strict app-store distribution rules controlled by Apple and Google.This is not the first time Musk has rejected the making of a phone-like AI hardware device.Speculation around “Starlink Phone” or “Tesla Pi Phone” have circulated for years. Musk has repeatedly made his feelings clear about entering the smartphone manufacturing market.“The idea of making a phone makes me want to die. But if we have to make a phone, we will," Musk said during an interview last October. Earlier this year, Musk pushed back against a Reuters report suggesting SpaceX was developing a handset to link directly with Starlink satellites, posting a firm, “We are not developing a phone” on social media.
Article Summary: Elon Musk responds to reports that SpaceX is developing an AI phone. The Wall Street Journal claimed that SpaceX recently demonstrated an early prototype to investors. The report also claimed that the device would run on a custom, proprietary operating system and rely on advanced AI from Musk’s AI startup, xAI.

Article Title: Tighter digital rules may hit startups: Report
Article Text:
digital declutter is the new way to remove unwanted stuff and maintain privacy

New Delhi: A more restrictive digital regulatory environment could slow India's startup momentum, reducing new venture creation by 20%, cutting annual venture capital investment by 25% and resulting in 245,000 fewer startup jobs by 2035, according to a report by Oxford Economics commissioned by Digital Prosperity Asia (DPA).The report, Digital Regulations and the Startup Ecosystem in India, is based on a survey of 550 ecosystem participants, including 350 startups, 100 venture capital firms and 100 incubators, along with interviews and economic modelling.According to the study, 88% of startups said digital regulations impose operational constraints, while 72% of startups and venture capital firms reported diverting resources away from research and innovation towards compliance-related activities. Nearly seven in ten startups said growing regulatory requirements have increased uncertainty around future returns, making fundraising and expansion more difficult.Oxford Economics estimates that if India shifts from its current relatively enabling regulatory framework to a more restrictive one between 2026 and 2035, it could lead to around 2,130 fewer startups being created every year. The report also projects an annual loss of about Rs 91,500 crore in venture capital investment during the period.The findings come at a time when India is positioning itself as one of the world's fastest-growing startup ecosystems and is seeking to attract global technology investment across sectors such as artificial intelligence, digital public infrastructure and deep technology.The report argues that overlapping regulations across areas such as artificial intelligence, data governance and cybersecurity risk increasing compliance costs and creating regulatory fragmentation, particularly for early-stage companies with limited resources.At the same time, it says an enabling regulatory approach could strengthen the ecosystem. Oxford Economics estimates that a more supportive policy environment could increase startup formation by 7%, raise annual venture capital investment by 9% and support an additional 80,000 startup jobs by 2035.The report also recommends adopting risk-based regulation for emerging technologies, improving coordination across digital regulatory frameworks and ensuring greater consultation with startups, investors and other ecosystem stakeholders while framing new rules. Such measures, it says, would help balance innovation with accountability without imposing unnecessary compliance burdens on young companies.
Article Summary: Report: A more restrictive digital regulatory environment could slow India's startup momentum. It could reduce new venture creation by 20%, cutting annual venture capital investment by 25% and resulting in 245,000 fewer startup jobs by 2035. 88% of startups said digital regulations impose operational constraints.

Article Title: In a nine-point manifesto, Palantir CEO Alex Karp to every company using AI: Do not hand your data to LLM companies, there is a reason why those selling tokens refuse to ...
Article Text:
Palantir CEO

The Trap of ' Tokenmaxxing '



Read Palantir’s 9-point notice posted on X:



Our thoughts on the importance of AI sovereignty.

1. Your AI sovereignty dictates your institution’s future. Sovereignty is the precondition for choice. Relinquishing sovereignty transfers the future choices of your institution to others, who are likely to exploit it for their gain and your loss.

2. Data retention is your treasure. Transfer it at your own peril. Your ability to win is dictated by your ability to recognize and use your unique edges, and you keep winning by compounding the underlying data to generate new insights. Transferring that data hands over access to your pre-existing winning plays and yields the means of production for new ones.

3. Tokenmaxxing hijacks your value orientation and decreases your institutional fortitude and intelligence. The pursuit of high token usage incentivizes disposable scripts over robust software — with the addictive feeling of false progress. There is a reason why those selling tokens refuse to charge based on value.

4. Controlling your weights is controlling your fate. Weights are the distilled form of hard-won, accumulated institutional knowledge. If you let others control your weights, you are allowing them to migrate the alpha of your business to theirs.

5. There is no contradiction between sovereignty and alpha. The architecture that maximally preserves sovereignty is one that enables institutions to own their tribal knowledge, and to compound it as alpha.

6. Politicizing the technical issues involving sovereignty is what your adversary wants. Techno-politicization is the wellspring of false sovereignty. Techno-politicization drives decisions that seem to reduce dependency, but ultimately limit agency — especially on the battlefield in the West.

7. Real expertise is existential. Allowing politics or favoritism to determine your technical decisions rewards whoever is best at politics, not whoever is right. Listen to those closest to the problems, not those speaking most compellingly about them.

8. Learn from institutions that are winning or that have consistently delivered. Institutions facing existential threats do not have the luxury of making technical decisions based on political preferences.

9. Only listen to institutions, countries, and people who have a proven record of being right. A track record of correctness is the best and only signal for future correctness. Judging something as right or wrong based on who you like is exceedingly misguided.

Palantir has released a nine-point manifesto targeting the artificial intelligence (AI) industry. The company warns corporations against handing over their proprietary data to elite Large Language Model (LLM) providers. In the statement published on X (formerly Twitter), the data analytics giant laid out its vision for “AI sovereignty” with a core message: keep your data strictly in-house, and do not outsource critical operations to commercial AI labs that Palantir says are untrustworthy.According to the manifesto, there is a strategic reason why tech companies selling “tokens”, which are the basic units of data processing used by LLMs” refuse to give up control, as they rely on corporate clients to feed and train their own models.The manifesto takes direct aim at American companies’ current spending frenzy on generative AI tools. Palantir said that the trend of “tokenmaxxing”, a term describing the practice of companies throwing as much money as possible at cloud computing and raw AI processing without a clear business strategy.Alex Karp has long been critical of the frontier AI labs. Earlier in June, he said on CNBC that the AI companies “don't understand how unlikeable they are”, adding that their products “don't actually work the way” customers expect.

Article Title: Quote of the day by Melinda French Gates, “We have to be careful in how we use this light shined on us”
Article Text:
Bill Gates and Melinda French Gates

Quote of the day by Melinda French Gates

What Melinda French Gates' quote means

A message reflected in her work

A simple takeaway



Melinda French Gates has spent decades thinking carefully about what it means to hold power, wealth, and public attention. The philanthropist and co-founder of the Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation has long been one of the most recognisable figures in global giving, and her quote on visibility and responsibility reflects a philosophy she has lived by throughout her public life. The message is simple but uncomfortably honest: being seen by the world is not a privilege to be enjoyed. It is a responsibility to be handled with care."We have to be careful in how we use this light shined on us."The quote is built around a single powerful image: a light being shined on someone. Gates is not talking about earned fame or deserved recognition. She is talking about the kind of attention that comes with wealth, platform, and influence, the kind that arrives not entirely because of what you have done but because of the position you occupy. The light, in her framing, belongs to the cause, not the person standing in it.What makes this quote worth sitting with is the word "careful." Not "grateful" for the light. Not "proud" of it. Careful. That is a deliberate choice, and it signals that Gates sees visibility as something that can be misused just as easily as it can be channelled for good. A public platform can amplify the right voices or drown them out. It can draw attention to what matters or redirect it toward the person holding the microphone.The responsibility, as she sees it, is to stay aware of that difference and make conscious choices about which way you are pulling.There is also an implicit humility embedded in the quote. By describing the light as being "shined on" her rather than earned by her, Gates acknowledges that people in her position did not manufacture their own visibility. It was given to them, in part by circumstance, by wealth, by marriage, and by the work of thousands of people inside the organisations they lead. That awareness changes how you behave when the cameras are on. It shifts the question from "what do I want to say?" to "who and what should I be amplifying right now?"This quote by Melinda French Gates perfectly goes with her approach towards philanthropy. After co-founding the Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation in 2000, Gates worked consistently to keep the focus on communities the foundation serves rather than on the institution or the individuals behind it. The Gates foundation also invested billions in global health, education and poverty reduction. The foundation also paid special attention towards maternal and child health in sub-Saharan Africa and South Asia.After her divorce from the Microsoft co-founder Bill Gates in 2021, Melinda French Gates launched Pivotal Ventures. For those unaware, Pivotal Ventures is an independent investment and incubation company, where Gates has directed significant resources toward expanding opportunities for women and families in the United States. Her caution about platform use is not abstract. It is evident in how she chooses to speak and when she chooses to step back.This quote by Melinda French Gates also offer something useful for anyone who finds themselves in a position of visibility, whether they lead a company, run a community group, or simply have a following on social media. Attention is a resource, and like any resource, it can be wasted or invested. Gates is suggesting that those who have it did not earn it alone, and the most honest thing they can do is use it for something larger than themselves. The light was not made for you. The question is what you illuminate with it.
Article Summary: Melinda French Gates has spent decades thinking carefully about what it means to hold power, wealth, and public attention. Her quote reflects a philosophy she has lived by throughout her public life. The message is simple but uncomfortably honest: being seen by the world is not a privilege to be enjoyed, it is a responsibility to be handled with care.
